title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
summary: The licensing, billing controls and rollout statements are supported by Microsoft's documentation and tenant notice. Minor corrections should complete two navigation paths, cite the spending-policy applicability table and flag the newer regional Claude guidance alongside the current data-boundary statement.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans access to usage-based billing models through the Chat model selector.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap targets General Availability for December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web platforms.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on November 4, 2026.
The roadmap says tenant admins must allocate credits for users to interact with the models.
claims.quote: Tenant admins will need to allocate credits so that users can interact with these models.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans requests to tenant admins after users consume their allotted credits.
claims.quote: If users consume their allotted credits, they will be able to request credits from their tenant admins.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: UBB experiences require a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage of UBB models consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: UBB is used in Copilot ... when working with newer agentic frontier models such as Astra and Fable. UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.claim: The feature has variable metered cost rather than subscription-only cost.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits. This model complements fixed subscription licensing

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The UBB models require admin-enabled UBB and provision of credits rather than access without billing setup.
claims.quote: Users will not have access to UBB models unless UBB is enabled. ... Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models. ... Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: spending policies
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Cost Management spending policies govern UBB models in Copilot Chat and Office.
claims.quote: Services managed by usage-based billing in the Microsoft admin center now include: ... Models with usage-based billing in Copilot Chat and Office
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits to sources; its services table explicitly lists 'Models with usage-based billing in Copilot Chat and Office'.

claims.claim: The USL covers everyday AI as a fixed-price foundation.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes UBB as covering advanced AI and frontier models beyond everyday USL AI.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.

claims.claim: Existing model choices are covered by the USL alongside the new UBB frontier choices.
claims.quote: Model selection is also part of the USL, with some models included with fair use, such as GPT 5.6 and Sonnet, and others included with limits, such as Opus.

claims.claim: MC1519122 names GPT-6 Astra as generally available with this UBB rollout.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout.

claims.claim: MC1519122 names Claude Fable 5.1 as generally available with this UBB rollout.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout.

claims.claim: MC1519122 preserves previously communicated eligibility requirements for the models.
claims.quote: Previously communicated eligibility requirements for these models apply.

claims.claim: The notice covers UBB model selection in Word, Excel and PowerPoint as well as Chat.
claims.quote: These models will be available from Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: The updated notice says users can set reasoning effort for a UBB model in Chat.
claims.quote: Additionally, users will be able to set the reasoning effort level when using a UBB model in Chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft plans in-product additional credit requests after the initial rollout.
claims.quote: After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.

claims.claim: MC1519122 does not give a date for the later credit-request capability.
claims.quote: We plan to rollout the ability for users to request credits from their tenant admins after this initial rollout.

claims.claim: The notice targets Frontier (Public) from early to mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: Frontier (Public): Beginning early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

claims.claim: The updated Worldwide GA window begins early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November)

claims.claim: The previously communicated GA start was early November.
claims.quote: Beginning in early December 2026 (previously early November)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude models are currently outside the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings ... are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
claims.fix: After the current EU Data Boundary statement, add: 'The EU/EFTA/UK apps guidance says Claude models are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026. It also recommends checking the Anthropic subprocessor setting before December 9, 2026: the apps-only option will disappear, and apps-only or unset selections will become All users; other selections, including No users, will not change.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps.

claims.claim: Claude models are currently excluded from applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Microsoft Product Terms and DPA apply when Anthropic operates as Microsoft's subprocessor, except for the separately labelled retention models.
claims.quote: Unless models are labeled "Anthropic models with Data Retention," the Microsoft Product Terms and Microsoft Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default.
claims.quote: have additional controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center and are off by default for all scenarios

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention require separate explicit tenant opt-in.
claims.quote: No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention fall under Anthropic's separate terms rather than Microsoft's Product Terms and DPA.
claims.quote: Anthropic acts as an independent processor and use of Anthropic models with Data Retention is subject to acceptance of Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service and Anthropic's Data Protection Addendum.

claims.claim: Some Fable-class models may have different or additional terms.
claims.quote: Certain Claude models, such as Fable 5.0 and Fable 5.1, may be made available to your organization with different or additional terms

claims.claim: Identity-based spending policies scope access by users or groups.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.

claims.claim: Moving between Entra ID groups causes the new group's spending policy to apply.
claims.quote: If a user moves from one Microsoft Entra ID group to another during a billing period, the new group's spending policy becomes effective for the user.

claims.claim: Consumption history carries forward when a user changes groups or policies.
claims.quote: the user's consumption history carries forward across the policy change. ... Moving a user between groups or spending policies doesn't reset the user's consumption.

claims.claim: Spending policies define access and spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits to users or groups.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.claim: Admins must configure a billing policy before users can use UBB-required AI experiences.
claims.quote: Admins must set up a billing policy before a user can use AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go bills credit consumption to the selected Azure subscription.
claims.quote: If you choose to override by using the pay-as-you-go option, the connected Azure subscription is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3) is a documented funding source.
claims.quote: You can purchase a Copilot Credit Pre-Purchase Plan (P3) from the Microsoft 365 admin center by selecting Buy Pre-purchase Credits

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing prepaid capacity packs can fund services managed in this billing experience.
claims.quote: If you purchased capacity packs, you can use them with the services in this experience.

claims.claim: P3 provides discounted commit units over a one-year term.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during a one-year term.

claims.claim: Usage beyond P3 credits can be billed pay-as-you-go when pay-as-you-go is enabled.
claims.quote: Usage beyond available pre-purchased credits can be billed as pay-as-you-go if pay-as-you-go is enabled.

claims.claim: Policies support monthly policy-level and per-user spending limits.
claims.quote: Select the monthly spending limit for this policy. ... Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). ... Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.claim: Alerts notify at configured thresholds.
claims.quote: Specify the usage threshold for the policy. ... Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.claim: On reaching the monthly policy limit users lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: A running task in a group spending policy can complete after exceeding the per-user limit.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn publishes no per-model Copilot Chat credit rate for GPT-6 Astra or Claude Fable 5.1 at the time checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable 5.1 model selector credit rates pricing; opened USL/UBB, setup, billing comparison, UBB overview and Copilot Studio billing rates. Studio rates describe Studio agents, not these Chat model interactions.

claims.claim: Government cloud rollout dates for this UBB model-selector feature are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable 5.1 model selector government GCC availability; read roadmap, MC1519122, UBB overview and Anthropic regional guidance. No government rollout date for this selector feature found.

claims.claim: Global and Billing administrators can add, select and change billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: The setup article says AI and License administrators can edit spending policies and manage limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The same article lists License Administrator among read-only reader roles, creating the inconsistency the briefing reports.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access

claims.claim: Spending policies, limits and alerts are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its table path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy'; the policy fly-out contains spending limits and alerts.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending-policy limits.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: periodLimit and perUserLimit set monthly policy and uniform per-user limits in the PATCH request body.
claims.quote: periodLimit ... The consumption limit for one period. A period is a UTC calendar month ... perUserLimit ... The uniform per-user consumption limit over the same period.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/spendingpolicy to sources; it defines the monthly period and the meaning of periodLimit and perUserLimit.

claims.claim: The spending-policy PATCH operation does not configure alerts.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Request eligibility is configured at Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Settings > All Settings. ... Select Access to usage-based billing experiences. ... under Choose who can request a spending policy
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and its table path to 'Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences > Choose who can request a spending policy'.

claims.claim: No automation for the tenant setting controlling who can request a spending policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Copilot access usage-based billing experiences request spending policy setting API; site:learn.microsoft.com Copilot Choose who can request a spending policy Graph API. Read access-request setting, UBB overview and spendingPolicy reference; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: Configuring access-request eligibility requires Global administrator.
claims.quote: To configure the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you need to be assigned to the Global administrator role.

claims.claim: Changes to access-request eligibility can take up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: Changes to this setting might take up to 24 hours to apply.

claims.claim: The request setting controls requests for a spending policy, not UBB setup or a model-hiding or blocking switch.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself. ... No users: Users cannot request a spending policy. Instead, they'll be presented with a link to learn more

claims.claim: The printed Anthropic provider-access path reaches the user/group selection control.
claims.quote: Copilot > Settings > View all. ... AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors ... under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences

claims.claim: No API equivalent for the Anthropic provider user-access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Copilot Anthropic AI provider users groups setting API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph copilot settings Anthropic subprocessor provider access users groups API. Read Anthropic subprocessor and apps guidance; results show UI and unrelated group APIs, not a provider-setting call.

claims.claim: The Anthropic provider-access control requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Anthropic provider control and its cited guidance concern Claude models rather than GPT-6 Astra.
claims.quote: You can restrict user access to AI provider subprocessors ... These assignments are applied at the provider level ... only the assigned users can use Copilot features or agents that rely on that AI provider.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta APIs can change and are unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > Top Actions > View requests opens the Credit requests page.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Overview tab. ... From the Top Actions section, you can View requests ... select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.

claims.claim: Whether later requests made from this Chat model selector reach the documented Credit requests page is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB model selector credit requests spending policy; read MC1519122, monitoring, USL/UBB, access-request setting and Copilot overview. Admin requests are documented generally, but this future selector-to-page route is not specified.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact; Open questions
claims.claim: How the Chat model selector presents these models to users without UBB access and credits is not established.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB model selector hide disabled models users without spending policy credit requests per model limits. Read access-request and discovery settings, Copilot overview, USL/UBB and MC1519122; no selector-specific hidden-versus-disabled presentation found.

claims.claim: Requests unmatched by a custom request policy continue through Microsoft's credit request service and can be resolved in the admin center.
claims.quote: Requests that don't match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The comparison article describes the admin view as credits-only rather than currency.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency. ... Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.

claims.claim: The monitoring article instead documents local-currency cost estimates including negotiated rates that might not match the bill.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.claim: The monitoring article distinguishes point-in-time exported reports from dashboard views retrieving live data.
claims.quote: Exported reports are generated as a point-in-time snapshot, while dashboard views continue to retrieve live data.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges for the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information ... Azure Cost Management doesn't show consumption against Prepaid Capacity packs. Use the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: An enabled Auto-apply new services setting automatically adds future supported services to a spending policy.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing discovery setting is deprecated.
claims.quote: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing setting is deprecated.

claims.claim: The deprecated discovery setting controls visibility of usage-based AI experiences.
claims.quote: this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.

claims.claim: Cost Management controls access and spending rather than merely discovery.
claims.quote: Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: UBB introduces consumption-driven interaction cost that varies with the work performed.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing means charges are based on the work performed rather than a flat per-user fee. The number of credits a task consumes varies with the models used

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: Support for per-model spending limits in this Chat selector is not established.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB model selector per model limits. Read setup, managing credits and spendingPolicy reference. Policy/per-user limits are documented; model templates currently apply only to Cowork, not this Chat selector.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows P3 purchase or amortized costs.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3) and Microsoft Agent pre-purchase plans (P3).

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity-pack consumption is monitored in Microsoft 365 or Power Platform rather than Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management doesn't show consumption against Prepaid Capacity packs. Use the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center, as applicable, to monitor Prepaid Capacity Pack credit usage.

claims.claim: The comparison article says dashboard totals and exports can be point-in-time views.
claims.quote: Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.

claims.claim: The supplied MC1519122 notice was updated on November 4, 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 4, 2026: We have updated the rollout schedule below.

claims.claim: The setup article says AI and License administrators cannot create spending policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies ... However, they can't create spending policies.
